A Cagey Opening Period The first half was a battle of attrition, with both sides struggling to find a clear opening. Twente looked the more threatening early on, as Sondre Oerjasaeter unleashed a powerful drive from distance in the 11th minute that whistled just wide of the post. Marko Pjaca kept the home defense on their toes with a series of dangerous corner deliveries, but SC Heerenveen remained organized. Bernt Klaverboer was called into action for routine collections, ensuring the game remained deadlocked as the teams headed into the tunnel for the break. Oyen Breaks the Deadlock The introduction of Luca Oyen at the start of the second half proved to be a masterstroke. Replacing Lanroy Machine , the substitute needed just six minutes to make his mark. In the 52nd minute, Jacob Trenskow found space to provide a perfectly weighted assist for Luca Oyen , who calmly slotted the ball home with his left foot. The goal shifted the momentum, forcing Twente to abandon their cautious approach and commit more players forward in search of an equalizer. Twente’s Late Surge and Defensive Resilience As the clock ticked down, Twente launched a relentless aerial assault. Younes Taha delivered a barrage of corners, testing the resolve of the SC Heerenveen backline. Headers from Max Bruns and Robin Propper forced saves from Bernt Klaverboer , who remained composed under immense pressure. The tension boiled over in stoppage time as Daan Rots received a yellow card for a reckless challenge, and Luca Oyen was booked for time-wasting. Despite a late chance for Wout Weghorst that flashed wide, the home side held firm to secure all three points.
